text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to close at $131.83, continuing a sharp two-week decline that's now totaled nearly 3%. The immediate driver is a retreat in oil prices: crude dropped significantly on September 17th after Saudi Arabia announced it would release additional supplies through the Strait of Hormuz to offset a pipeline attack, easing supply-disruption fears. Even though geopolitical tensions remain high—with fresh attacks between Saudi Arabia and Houthis reported this week and smoke and flames near Riyadh's airport on September 19th—the market is pricing in less actual supply loss than it initially feared.

The broader context here is a widening gap between physical oil supply risk and actual price impact. While Middle East conflict continues to generate headlines, traders are focusing on the concrete reality that key producers can reroute exports and offset disruptions, which takes the edge off panic-driven rallies in oil prices that would normally lift energy stocks.
